# moe.platform.ios

Produces `moe-ios.jar` — the iOS framework bindings (UIKit, Metal, GameController, …) that user apps consume.

## What's in `src/main/java/apple/**`

**Checked-in generated code with manual fixes layered on top.** Generated by NatJGen from iOS SDK headers; the manual fixes are captured as `fix_manual_binding_changes.patch` so a regen + re-apply cycle produces the same checked-in tree.

The lifecycle build only `javac`'s these sources. NatJGen does **not** run during a normal build.

## When and how to regenerate

Manual one-shot, not part of any normal build:

```
./gradlew :moe-core:moe.apple:moe.platform.ios:generateBindings
```

It runs `org.moe.natjgen.Main` (from `:moe.generator.natjgen`) against the `platform.natjgen` config, with `java.library.path` set to `prebuilts/llvm/macos/lib` (libclang.dylib) and `natj/natj-mac/build/xcode/Release` (libnatj.dylib). Output is generated source overwriting `src/main/java/apple/**`. After regeneration, `git apply fix_manual_binding_changes.patch` is the convenience that re-applies hand-tuned fixes.

The full ritual (regenerate → apply patch → fix new mismatches → update patch) is in `UPDATE_IOS_BINDING.md`. Engine internals are covered by the `moe-natjgen` skill.

## Helper scripts

- `platform_natjgen_updater.py` — `:updateNatJGenConfig` task. Refreshes `platform.natjgen` against the active iOS SDK before a regen.
- `remove_deprecated_files.py` — `:removeOutdatedBindings` task. Reads `build/generate_bindings.log` to delete generated files for symbols no longer in the SDK.
- `check_moved_files.py` — sanity-check helper for binding moves between SDK versions.

## The fat-jar quirk is intentional

`tasks.jar { from(configurations.runtimeClasspath.get().map { ... zipTree(it) }) }` packages NatJ runtime classes into `moe-ios.jar`. This is deliberate — license isolation + simpler consumption — not an oversight. Don't refactor to a thin jar without coordination.

## spotless

`spotless.java { target("src/main/java/apple/**"); eclipse().configFile("Eclipse_Adjusted_NatJGen.xml") }` formats only the generated tree. The Eclipse formatter config matches what JDT emits, so `generateBindings` + `spotlessApply` together produce a stable shape.
